text:
sara-liu: FYI - GitHub security advisory just hit: CVE-2026-2109 affecting kubelet providers, exploited in the wild. Advisory: https://sec.example.com/advisories/CVE-2026-2109 :rotating_light: we need an emergency mitigation plan.
sec-bot: Auto advisory posted: CVE-2026-2109 - privilege escalation via module load path (confirmed in the wild). Patch available in upstream kubelet v1.27.6 and v1.28.2. See https://kubernetes.io/security
alex-garcia: thanks. quick Q: do we have public-facing node kubelet ports? list says some EKS clusters still have 10250 open to mgmt VPCs.
mike-choi: Confirmed two edge clusters have kubelet read/write exposed through old firewall rules. I'm isolating now.
jamie-obrien: Immediate mitigation checklist suggestion: 1) Block access to kubelet port 10250 from non-admin subnets (security groups / firewall); 2) Apply kubelet upgrade to patched builds on canary nodes; 3) Enable audit rules to detect insmod/modprobe; 4) Cordon & drain high-risk nodes for patching. thoughts?
sara-liu: +1 on checklist. Also we should enforce RBAC to deny DaemonSets from creating privileged hostPath mounts while we triage.
alex-garcia: working on SG changes now. Pushing rule to block 10250 from all subnets except admin-bastion -> will take ~8 mins to propagate.
mike-choi: On the audit side, here's quick auditctl rule to capture module loads on linux nodes:

```
# capture insmod/rmmod/modprobe
auditctl -w /sbin/insmod -p x -k modload
auditctl -w /sbin/rmmod -p x -k modload
auditctl -w /sbin/modprobe -p x -k modload
```

I'll push via the node init daemonset to canary group.
jamie-obrien: Good. Also add a k8s audit policy to log Pod/CRI operations that call /exec or device node mounts. Start with high verbosity for 24h.
ops-oncall: I've queued canary cordon/drain for cluster-edge-3 and edge-standby-1. ETA for patch deploy to canary: 22 minutes.
elaine-legal: Heads up — security comms will need an internal incident notice and an external customer advisory template. I'll draft internal comms once we have the mitigations & exposure estimate.
sara-liu: Who can run a quick inventory of clusters with nodes running container runtimes with CAP_SYS_MODULE or privileged DaemonSets?
alex-garcia: Running query now. kubectl + label filter across clusters. Quick grep shows ~7 nodes with running privileged DaemonSets that mount /lib/modules.

Command used:
```
kubectl get ds --all-namespaces -o=jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}:{.metadata.name}:{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].securityContext.privileged}\n{end}'
```

I'll paste results in #eng-sre also.
mike-choi: For nodes where we can't reboot immediately, we can reduce risk by removing the Kubelet credentials from any non-admin service accounts and revoking the kubelet bootstrap tokens. But that may impact autoscaling.
jamie-obrien: Agree, prefer firewall lock + RBAC changes first to avoid service disruption. Then upgrade canaries, validate, and bulk rollout.
sara-liu: Patch timeline: canaries -> 6 clusters in wave 1 (low-traffic) -> remaining in wave 2. Need rollback plan if kernel module load behavior differs.
ops-oncall: Canary patch completed on edge-3. Post-upgrade smoke: node kubelet logs look normal, no crash loops. No module-loading alerts triggered (expected: blocked by patched kubelet).
sec-bot: Note: upstream recommends also setting the kubelet flag --protect-kernel-modules (or similar). Check patched flag name before rollout.
alex-garcia: I couldn't find that exact flag in docs. Likely advisory shorthand. We'll rely on upgraded kubelet build from upstream; building custom flags introduces risk.
mike-choi: Capture audit logs to long-term storage for post-incident forensics. Suggest shipping modload audit events to our centralized Splunk index under index=sec_audit.
jamie-obrien: Add detector rule: if audit.log contains syscall=init_module or syscall=finit_module from non-root container user namespaces => high priority alert.
sara-liu: ops-oncall, once wave1 validated, start wave2 at 01:00 UTC. I'll own comms to customers after legal signs off.
elaine-legal: Draft internal notice ready. For external: we will offer a recommended mitigation matrix and mention nodes patched to v1.27.6+ / v1.28.2+. Need confirmation of affected regions.
ops-oncall: Wave1 complete. Wave2 starting now. Rolling upgrade pace ~1 cluster per 6 minutes. ETA completion: 2 hours.
alex-garcia: Firewall rules propagated. Kubelet API no longer reachable from mgmt subnets except admin-bastion.
mike-choi: Audit rule deployed to canaries and forwarded to Splunk. Example alert snippet I pushed:

```
index=sec_audit modload | stats count by host, pid, uid
```

So far zero modload entries since mitigation.
jamie-obrien: Post-mortem notes to capture: why were kubelet ports reachable, why DaemonSets with host mounts allowed, why image signing not enforced for modules. Add these to incident backlog.
sara-liu: Good. After wave2 finishes, let's rotate any kubelet bootstrap tokens and rotate node SSH keys for clusters we found privileged DS on.
ops-oncall: Wave2 done. All clusters upgraded to patched kubelet. No active exploitation detected in our logs. Marking incident as mitigated.
elaine-legal: Internal memo ready. External advisory draft ready — legal + security review needed. @sara-liu please approve wording, then I'll coordinate CS message.
sara-liu: Approved. Thank you everyone. Follow-up actions assigned in Triage board. :white_check_mark:
sec-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. All artifacts archived to /sec/incidents/CVE-2026-2109/ (internal).
